title: THERMOSTAT: Elastic RICE with Latency & Cost Attenuation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and validate a prioritization variant that preserves RICE interpretability but systematically penalizes features that materially increase latency or per-unit cost. Deliver a repeatable scoring recipe, worked examples, an automated spreadsheet/script, and recommended integration into the quarterly roadmap reviews and OKR intake flow.
background: Current RICE outputs at Redwood often promote high-reach/high-impact work without adequately accounting for downstream inference economics (token cost) or user experience regressions (tail latency). Existing sheets (see PM-5172) contain separate latency/cost matrices but lack a single, auditable score that balances revenue/impact with operational economics. This ticket proposes THERMOSTAT: an Elastic RICE variant that attenuates RICE scores using normalized latency and cost signals so product trade-offs are explicit during scoping and OKR tradeoff sessions.
proposed_scoring_formula:
Base_RICE = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort.
Normalize latency and cost into [0,1] where 0 = baseline (no additional impact) and 1 = worst-acceptable.
Attenuation = 1 / (1 + alpha * Latency_norm + beta * Cost_norm).
Final_Score = Base_RICE * Attenuation.
Recommended defaults: alpha=1.2, beta=0.8 (tunable by initiative type). Provide both per-request latency_norm (p95 delta relative to current) and per-token cost_norm (expected incremental $/1M tokens relative to baseline).
scoring_examples: Example A (Small UX improvement): Reach=200k users, Impact=3, Confidence=0.8, Effort=5 -> Base_RICE=(200000*3*0.8)/5=96,000. Latency_delta p95=+10ms -> Latency_norm=0.1; Cost_delta=+$0.02 per 1k tokens -> Cost_norm=0.05. Attenuation=1/(1+1.2*0.1+0.8*0.05)=0.88. Final_Score~84,480.

Example B (New capability using larger model): Reach=80k, Impact=6, Confidence=0.6, Effort=8 -> Base_RICE=36,000. Latency_delta p95=+80ms -> Latency_norm=0.6; Cost_delta=+$0.50 per 1k tokens -> Cost_norm=0.7. Attenuation=1/(1+1.2*0.6+0.8*0.7)=0.51. Final_Score~18,360.

Example C (Ops reliability work): Reach=internal only (10k), Impact=2, Confidence=0.9, Effort=3 -> Base_RICE=6,000. Latency_norm=0 (no user-facing latency), Cost_norm=0. Attenuation=1. Final_Score=6,000. Shows ops can still surface when cost/latency are neutral.
decision_records: Normalize latency using p95 delta relative to the relevant baseline route/endpoint; use historical 90-day tail as baseline for new features.
Normalize cost using expected incremental $/1M tokens or $/month for the customer segment; map worst-acceptable to 1.0 and baseline to 0.0.
Alpha (latency weight) and Beta (cost weight) default to 1.2 and 0.8 respectively; adjust per-initiative taxonomy (e.g., client-facing vs backend infra).
Keep RICE interpretability: report Base_RICE and Attenuation separately in the tracker and allow override notes for business cases.
acceptance_criteria: A documented formula (above) exists in Confluence with rationale and parameter definitions.
A prioritized worksheet (Google Sheet) and an executable script (Python) that calculates Final_Score for a list of candidate initiatives is published and linked from the ticket.
Three pilot initiatives (one UX, one new capability, one infra) are scored and presented at the next roadmap review with sensitivity analysis on alpha/beta.
Guidance and a short checklist for PMs to estimate latency_norm and cost_norm are included so scoring is repeatable.
Integration plan documented for how Final_Score vs Base_RICE will be surfaced in quarterly OKR intake and executive summaries.
implementation_steps: Draft Confluence page with formula, normalization rules, and examples (owner: Maya).
Build Google Sheet template with normalized input fields and computed Base_RICE, Attenuation, Final_Score; add comments/tooltips (owner: Liam).
Implement Python script and small CLI to compute scores from CSV exports; add unit tests for normalization edge-cases (owner: Data PM engineer).
Run scoring pilot on three initiatives and prepare a 15-min walkthrough for roadmap review (owner: Liam & Maya).
Collect feedback, adjust alpha/beta, finalize defaults, and publish versioned scoring guide (owner: Product Ops).
Add a lightweight automation to attach computed scores to roadmap tickets in our product tracker (follow-up ticket after pilot).
